title: The Storyteller's Quill
welcome_lead: Meet the protagonist of your own quest and learn who tells the tale.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on character types and narrator voices.
final_note: You can now name the hero and the voice that guides the story.

walkthroughs.body_html: The protagonist drives the story; the antagonist stands in the way. In Harry Potter, Harry is the protagonist and Voldemort the antagonist. Conflict between them powers the plot.
Direct: 'She was kind.' Indirect: 'She shared her lunch with the new boy.' Indirect characterisation lets readers infer traits from behaviour and dialogue.
A 1st-person narrator says 'I'. A 3rd-person omniscient narrator knows every character's thoughts. A 3rd-person limited narrator follows one character. An unreliable narrator may distort the truth.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a metaphor and a simile?
options: Metaphors are short and similes are long.
A simile compares using 'like' or 'as'; a metaphor states one thing IS another, making an implicit comparison without those connectives.
